questions.question: A car covers $AB$ distance with first one-third at velocity {v}_{1}{ms}^{ - 1}$, second one-third at {v}_{2}{ms}^{ - 1}$ and last one-third at {v}_{3}{ms}^{ - 1}$. If {v}_{3} = 3{v}_{1},{v}_{2} = 2{v}_{1}$ and {v}_{1} = 11{ms}^{ - 1}$, then the average velocity of the car is _____ {ms}^{ - 1}$.
questions.explanation:
Let the total distance be $d$.

Time taken to cover {\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)}^{\mathrm{rd}}$ of total distance is {t}_{1} = \frac{d}{3{v}_{1}}$.

Time taken to cover {\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)}^{\mathrm{rd}}$ of total distance is {t}_{2} = \frac{d}{3{v}_{2}}$.

Time taken to cover {\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)}^{\mathrm{rd}}$ of total distance is {t}_{3} = \frac{d}{3{v}_{3}}$.

Average speed$= \frac{\mathrm{Total}\mathrm{distance}}{\mathrm{Total}\mathrm{time}} {v}_{avg} = \frac{d}{\frac{d}{3{v}_{1}} + \frac{d}{3{v}_{2}} + \frac{d}{3{v}_{3}}} \implies {v}_{avg} = \frac{3\left({v}_{1}{v}_{2}{v}_{3}\right)}{{v}_{1}{v}_{2} + {v}_{2}{v}_{3} + {v}_{3}{v}_{1}}$

Here, {v}_{1} = 11m{s}^{ - 1}$, then, {v}_{3} = 33m{s}^{ - 1},{v}_{2} = 22m{s}^{ - 1} {V}_{\mathrm{avg}} = \frac{3 \times 11 \times 22 \times 33}{\left(11 \times 22\right) + \left(22 \times 33\right) + \left(33 \times 11\right)} = 18m{s}^{ - 1}$

questions.explanation:
The time $\left({t}_{1}\right)$ taken by the person to travel distance $x$ with velocity {v}_{1}$ is given by

{t}_{1} = \frac{x}{{v}_{1}}...\left(1\right)$

The time $\left({t}_{2}\right)$ taken by the person to travel distance $x$ with velocity {v}_{2}$ is given by

{t}_{2} = \frac{x}{{v}_{2}}...\left(2\right)$

The formula to calculate the average speed $\left(v\right)$ of the person is given by

$v = \frac{2x}{{t}_{1} + {t}_{2}}...\left(3\right)$

Substitute the expressions from equations (1) and (2) into equation (3) to obtain the required relation.

$\begin{matrix}v & = & \frac{2x}{\left(\frac{x}{{v}_{1}} + \frac{x}{{v}_{2}}\right)} \\ & \implies & \frac{x}{{v}_{1}} + \frac{x}{{v}_{2}} = \frac{2x}{v} \\ & \implies & \frac{2}{v} = \frac{1}{{v}_{1}} + \frac{1}{{v}_{2}}\end{matrix}$

questions.question: An object moves with speed {v}_{1},{v}_{2}\text{and}{v}_{3}$ along a line segment $AB,BC\text{and}CD$ respectively as shown in figure. Where $AB = BC\text{and}AD = 3AB$, then average speed of the object will be :
questions.explanation:
Speed of an object is defined as the distance travelled by the object per unit time.

Let's assume that, $AB = d$. So, $BC = d,AD = 3d$. Also, assume that the time required by the object to travel $AB,BC,CD$ are {t}_{1},{t}_{2},{t}_{3}$ respectively.

Now,

$\begin{matrix}AD & = & 3AB \\ AB + BC + CD & = & 3AB \\ AB + AB + CD & = & 3AB \\ CD & = & AB\end{matrix}$

Hence,

$\begin{matrix}{t}_{1} & = & \frac{AB}{{v}_{1}} \\ & = & \frac{d}{{v}_{1}} \\ {t}_{2} & = & \frac{d}{{v}_{2}} \\ {t}_{3} & = & \frac{d}{{v}_{3}}\end{matrix}$

The formula to calculate the average speed $\left({v}_{a}\right)$ of the object is given by

{v}_{a} = \frac{AD}{{t}_{1} + {t}_{2} + {t}_{3}}........................(1)$

Substitute the expressions for the parameters into equation (1) and simplify to obtain the required average speed of the object.

$\begin{matrix}{v}_{a} & = & \frac{3d}{\frac{d}{{v}_{1}} + \frac{d}{{v}_{2}} + \frac{d}{{v}_{3}}} \\ & = & \frac{3{v}_{1}{v}_{2}{v}_{3}}{{v}_{1}{v}_{2} + {v}_{2}{v}_{3} + {v}_{3}{v}_{1}}\end{matrix}$

$\implies \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} = \frac{{t}_{1}}{{t}_{1} + {t}_{2}} \implies 1 + \frac{{t}_{2}}{{t}_{1}} = \sqrt{2} \implies \frac{{t}_{1}}{{t}_{2}} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2} - 1}$

Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is correct but Statement II is false
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is true
questions.explanation:
The definition of displacement is given by the product of velocity and time.

$\int vdt = \Delta x =$displacement of body in given time.

Thus, the area under the velocity time graph gives the displacement of the body and the area under the acceleration time graph gives the change in velocity of the body.
